description:
TwinTech is an engineering duo of final-year CS students from India (SCAD CET) building software for NASA’s Artemis missions.

Jeffrey Ryan R — Systems & Telemetry Lead: 1st Place VISAI Hackathon winner. Built the full-stack cockpit, live NASA JPL Horizons API pipeline, and 14-day Golden Window timeline.

Imaya Thillai S — Geospatial & Math Lead: ISRO Space Hackathon participant. Engineered the 360° LOLA horizon raymarching, lunar curvature drop math, and Kaggle crater hazard model.
summary:
When planning a lunar landing at the Moon's South Pole, mission success hinges on an unforgiving geometric reality: because the Moon has almost zero axial tilt (1.54°), the Sun grazes the horizon at just 1.5° to 3° above the terrain. Mountain ridges and crater rims cast long shadows stretching dozens of kilometers, while deep crater topography frequently severs Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio contact.
We developed SeleneSight, an open-source web application that reconstructs the 360° local topographic horizon for any South Pole landing site using NASA LOLA 30m altimetry models. By calculating the apparent topocentric trajectories of both the Sun and Earth, SeleneSight dynamically detects when mountain silhouettes cause solar eclipses or communication blackouts. 
The tool introduces an interactive 14-day concurrency timeline that automatically identifies "Golden Windows"—rare operational periods where surface landers have simultaneous battery-charging sunlight and active radio links to the Deep Space Network. Cross-referencing NASA's 13 official Artemis III candidate zones and the 1.3-million-crater Robbins database from Kaggle, SeleneSight gives mission controllers, CLPS commercial landers, and educators a fast,
details:
SELENESIGHT: LUNAR SOUTH POLE LANDING & TRAJECTORY NAVIGATOR

WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

SeleneSight is an end-to-end mission planning and terrain obstruction intelligence platform engineered for NASA's Artemis III/IV human landing missions and Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) robotic landers targeting the Moon's South Pole (80°S to 90°S).

It operates through five interconnected technical innovations:

• 360° Radial Horizon Raymarching: Surrounding crater rims and massifs cast shadows for dozens of kilometers. SeleneSight casts radial rays across all 360 azimuthal degrees (up to 30 km) against NASA LRO LOLA 30m Digital Elevation Models (SLDEM2015). It applies a quadratic spherical lunar curvature correction: tan(Elevation) = (Feature Height - Observer Height) / Distance - d² / (2 * R_moon), ensuring distant peaks like Malapert Mountain (+5,040 m) do not appear artificially towering.

• Topocentric Ephemeris & Libration Engine: Because the Moon's axial tilt is only 1.54°, the Sun skims the horizon at graze angles of just 1.5° to 3.0°. Our engine tracks apparent solar elevation and models Earth's apparent wobble caused by lunar libration (±6.68° latitude, ±7.91° longitude), dynamically verifying direct line-of-sight to NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) ground stations.

• The "Golden Window" Concurrency Algorithm: Solar-powered landers need sunlight to recharge batteries, but also require an open radio link to Earth to downlink science. SeleneSight overlays both tracks across a 14-day synodic cycle (336 hours at 2-hour increments) to pinpoint the "Golden Windows"—the exact hours where power and communications are simultaneously uninterrupted.

• Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) Scoring: Evaluates landing feasibility across 5 weighted dimensions: solar uptime, DTE radio link, touchdown slope safety (<5° nominal), volatile ice proximity, and crater rim clearance.

• Automated NASA Flight Readiness Review (FRR) Generator: Automatically compiles landing ellipse coordinates, slope hazard envelopes, and communication schedules into an audit-ready, printable NASA mission directive.


WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

• Prevents Mission-Ending Tip-Overs: In February 2024, Intuitive Machines' Odysseus (IM-1) lander touched down on an unmodeled 12° slope near Malapert A, breaking a landing leg and tipping on its side. SeleneSight calculates local slope gradients and crater ejecta boulder risks to keep landers within safe tolerances (<5° average, >12° hazard cutoff).

• Eliminates Command-Line Complexity: Legacy tools like NAIF SPICE kernels and desktop-bound Horizon software require specialized programming and steep learning curves. SeleneSight brings mission-grade analysis into a modern web browser running client-side at 60 FPS with zero installation.

• Compresses Trade Studies from Weeks to Seconds: Flight controllers can evaluate all 13 official Artemis III candidate zones across varying launch dates (2026–2028), reducing mission feasibility analysis time by over 95%.

WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

• Immediate Operational Impact: Securing early Artemis III and CLPS commercial lander survival by ensuring surface assets land during optimum Golden Windows, keeping batteries charged and communications open.

• Long-Term Lunar Base Camp Selection: Pinpointing ridges of near-permanent illumination (such as Shackleton Connecting Ridge) to establish long-duration habitats and cryogenic propellant depots.

• Surface Rover Traverse Routing: Providing dynamic shadow-avoidance pathfinding for Lunar Terrain Vehicles (LTV) traveling between dark cold-trap ice deposits and sunlit charging ridges.

• Deep Space Exploration Transfer: Serving as an adaptable mathematical baseline for exploring deep polar craters on Mars (such as Korolev Crater).

WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

• Frontend & Architecture: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

• Data Sources & Telemetry APIs:

->NASA JPL Horizons REST API for real-time topocentric azimuth and elevation vectors.

->NASA Solar System Treks (Moon Trek) OGC-compliant WMTS tile services for South Pole stereographic cartography.

->NASA LRO LOLA PDS Geosciences Archive (SLDEM2015 30m) for topographic height profiling.

->Stuart Robbins Lunar Crater Database (1.3M+ Craters via Kaggle) for crater rim buffering and morphology analysis.

->Kaggle LU3M6TGT Object Detection Dataset for rock abundance fractional area modeling.

• Deployment & Performance: Deployed on Vercel Edge Network with sub-100ms global latency; client-side vector mathematics optimized to prevent browser main-thread blocking.

HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

Rather than creating another static dashboard with pre-rendered maps, SeleneSight approaches the lunar South Pole as a living, dynamic environment:

• The 360° Local Sky Panorama: Translates complex mathematical elevation rasters into an intuitive mountain skyline where mission planners can watch the Sun and Earth rise and dip behind real crater rims.

• The "Golden Window" Metric: Synthesizes two disconnected operational constraints (solar battery charging vs. radio line-of-sight) into a clear visual timeline that anyone from a NASA flight director to a student can understand instantly.

• Fail-Safe Two-Tier Architecture: Pre-caches the 13 Artemis III candidate sites for instant 0ms demo exploration, while providing a live coordinate dropper that queries real NASA JPL Horizons REST endpoints on demand.

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

• Spherical Lunar Curvature Drop: The Moon's radius (1,737 km) is only a quarter of Earth's, causing the surface to fall away rapidly. Without applying d² / (2 * R_moon), distant mountain rims appear artificially tall and distorted; our raymarching incorporates the exact drop curve.

• Earth Libration Wobble: Viewed from 89°S, the Earth does not sit still—it oscillates in an apparent ellipse driven by lunar libration in latitude (±6.68°) and longitude (±7.91°). A 2° wobble is the difference between a direct radio link to DSN Goldstone and a total blackout behind a mountain ridge.

• Touchdown Slope Margins: Cross-referencing recent missions like IM-1 at Malapert A confirmed that landing on slopes above 8° presents severe tip-over hazards; SeleneSight scores slope gradients conservatively to ensure lander stability.

• Artemis Accords & Open Science: Designed to support peaceful mission deconfliction (Section 11) and lunar heritage preservation (Section 9) by making mission planning accessible, transparent, and 100% open-source.

Live Application: https://selenesight.vercel.app
